reader.requirement: DIVIDE format 4 (INTO ... GIVING identifier-3 [ROUNDED] REMAINDER identifier-4) stores the quotient of operand 2 / operand 1 in the one identifier-3, then the remainder (dividend minus the truncated, unedited quotient with identifier-3's digits, decimal point and sign presence times the divisor, GR6) in identifier-4 by truncation (GR7), with identifier-4's subscript evaluated just before that store; under ON SIZE ERROR a quotient size error leaves both and a remainder size error leaves identifier-4 (GR8); the witness covers integer and one-decimal unsigned items and the subscript timing.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectLevel < 2002 with an unsigned fixed-point identifier-3: the subsidiary quotient takes the absolute value (§1985 GR6 'same presence or absence of a sign'); 2002+ keeps it signed
UnphrasedSizeErrorIsFatal by DialectLevel: 1985 catches an unphrased zero divisor and continues with both receivers unchanged

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel|Edition in ArithmeticEmitter.cs (lines 264, 719) and ArithmeticBinder.cs (none); ResolveReceivingAtStore/IdentifiedAtStore carry no edition test.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: an unsigned identifier-3 with a negative quotient forms the remainder from the magnitude at 1985 and from the signed quotient at 2002+; the unphrased zero divisor continues at 1985 and is fatal at 2023
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf14_04 L6-L8 cover unsigned positive operands and the identifier-4 subscript; negative operands, ROUNDED, edited identifier-3/4 and the GR8 size-error halves are not exercised there (pb5182 witness and probes here)

reader.notes: identifier-4 is resolved through ResolveReceivingAtStore so its subscript is identified at the store; the quotient is stored first and the remainder store is gated on the size-error flag under the phrase. The one 1985 arm (UnsignedSubsidiary) implements GR6's sign clause and is witnessed by pb5182 and dzero NEG.
